title: Hong Kong outbreak analysis reveals growing role of norovirus - foodsafetynews.com

analysis.location_and_population: Skip to content Sign Up for Free FSN Weekly Newsletter Trusted by 45,000+ food safety leaders, regulators, and professionals.
analysis.event: Analysis of norovirus outbreaks over a decade in Hong Kong, reported by Food Safety News, highlighting the growing prevalence of norovirus-related raw oyster outbreaks.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 1,964 norovirus outbreaks recorded from 2016 to 2025 in Hong Kong, with a growing role of raw oyster-associated transmission.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report is an analysis of historical outbreak data; no active public-health response actions are described. The analysis underscores the need for continued surveillance and targeted interventions in food safety, particularly concerning raw oyster consumption.

analysis.brief_en: An analysis published on 11 August 2026 by Food Safety News reveals that norovirus outbreaks linked to raw oyster consumption have become increasingly prevalent in Hong Kong over the past decade. Between 2016 and 2025, Hong Kong recorded 1,964 norovirus outbreaks, with the data indicating a growing role of raw oysters as a transmission vehicle. The study highlights the importance of strengthening food safety measures and surveillance to mitigate the risk of norovirus gastroenteritis associated with high-risk food items. While the analysis provides critical insights into the epidemiology of norovirus in the region, it does not detail immediate public-health interventions or outbreak response actions.

title: Over a hundred norovirus cases hit the cruise ship "Caribbean Princess" during Caribbean voyage - Puente de Mando

analysis.time: Published on 2026-08-08; event occurred during the cruise voyage from April 28 to May 11, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Cruise ship 'Caribbean Princess' (Bermuda-flagged) during a Caribbean voyage, with cases reported among passengers and crew.
analysis.event: A norovirus outbreak causing acute gastroenteritis was reported aboard the cruise ship 'Caribbean Princess' by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 115 individuals affected: 102 passengers and 13 crew members out of 3,116 passengers, with symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea. The cruise line described cases as mild and limited.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The cruise line Princess Cruises stated the outbreak involved a limited number of mild cases and that the ship would undergo thorough cleaning and disinfection before its next itinerary. The CDC reported the outbreak.

analysis.brief_en: A norovirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship 'Caribbean Princess' during a Caribbean voyage has sickened 115 people, including 102 passengers and 13 crew members, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The outbreak occurred during a voyage that departed Fort Lauderdale on April 28 and concluded in Port Canaveral on May 11, 2026. Symptoms reported were primarily vomiting and diarrhea, and the cruise operator described the cases as mild and limited in number. Princess Cruises confirmed the ship will undergo enhanced cleaning and disinfection before resuming operations.
analysis.summary_en: A norovirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship 'Caribbean Princess' during a Caribbean voyage has sickened 115 people, including 102 passengers and 13 crew members, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The outbreak occurred during a voyage that departed Fort Lauderdale on April 28 and concluded in Port Canaveral on May 11, 2026. Symptoms reported were primarily vomiting and diarrhea, and the cruise operator described the cases as mild and limited in number. Princess Cruises confirmed the ship will undergo enhanced cleaning and disinfection before resuming operations.

title: Korea Food Poisoning Cases Jump 28% as Salmonella, Norovirus Surge - Seoul Economic Daily

analysis.location_and_population: Republic of Korea (South Korea); outbreaks reported nationwide with regional data for Gyeonggi, Busan, Seoul, Daejeon, Jeju, and North Chungcheong.
analysis.event: Reported increase in food poisoning outbreaks and cases in 2025 compared to 2024, attributed to Salmonella and norovirus; official data released by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 319 outbreaks and 9,780 patients in 2025, a 20% rise in outbreaks and 28% rise in patients compared to 2024 (265 outbreaks, 7,624 patients). Salmonella accounted for 79 outbreaks and 4,248 patients (43% of total); norovirus accounted for 68 outbreaks (31 more than 2024). Eggs were implicated in 14 outbreaks with 2,392 patients (24% of total). Restaurants accounted for 192 outbreaks (over 60% of total). Regional risk per million population highest in Daejeon (685), Jeju (479), and North Chungcheong (375).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety recommended handwashing after handling eggs and cooking food to at least 75°C for one minute; emphasized blocking cross-contamination with eggs to prevent Salmonella. Plans include expanding advance inspections of vulnerable facilities and tailored preventive publicity. Seasonal patterns noted: bacterial food poisoning peaks in summer, viral (including norovirus) in winter. Data reflects official surveillance; no indication of underreporting adjustments.

analysis.brief_en: South Korea’s food poisoning cases surged 28% in 2025, with 9,780 patients and 319 outbreaks reported by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. Salmonella and norovirus were the leading causes, with Salmonella responsible for 4,248 cases (43% of total) and norovirus for 68 outbreaks. Restaurants accounted for over 60% of outbreaks, while eggs were implicated in 14 outbreaks affecting 2,392 people. Regional risk per million population was highest in Daejeon, Jeju, and North Chungcheong. Authorities urged improved hygiene and cooking practices, including handwashing after handling eggs and heating food to 75°C for at least one minute, and announced plans to expand targeted inspections and public awareness campaigns.
analysis.summary_en: South Korea’s food poisoning cases surged 28% in 2025, with 9,780 patients and 319 outbreaks reported by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. Salmonella and norovirus were the leading causes, with Salmonella responsible for 4,248 cases (43% of total) and norovirus for 68 outbreaks. Restaurants accounted for over 60% of outbreaks, while eggs were implicated in 14 outbreaks affecting 2,392 people. Regional risk per million population was highest in Daejeon, Jeju, and North Chungcheong. Authorities urged improved hygiene and cooking practices, including handwashing after handling eggs and heating food to 75°C for at least one minute, and announced plans to expand targeted inspections and public awareness campaigns.

title: Over a dozen sickened in fourth gastrointestinal illness outbreak on cruise ship in two months - AOL.com

analysis.time: Published 2026-08-11; event occurred during the July 15, 2026 voyage.
analysis.location_and_population: National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship; voyage route included Ketchikan, Alaska; affected population: 57 guests and crew members.
analysis.event: Reported gastrointestinal illness outbreak on a cruise ship; the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed the event; cause remains under investigation.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Eight of 57 guests and five crew members reported illness; symptoms included abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea; cause unknown; nine gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships reported to CDC so far in 2026, with five attributed to norovirus, two to E. coli, and two still unknown.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Lindblad Expeditions and crew increased cleaning and disinfection, isolated ill passengers and crew, consulted the CDC Vessel Sanitation Program, paused passenger operations, and canceled three subsequent voyages to conduct enhanced sanitation protocols; ship en route to Ketchikan, Alaska.

analysis.brief_en: A gastrointestinal illness outbreak sickened 13 people—eight guests and five crew—aboard the National Geographic Sea Bird during a July 15 voyage, marking the vessel’s fourth such incident in under two months. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed the cases, which featured abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea, but the cause remains undetermined. In response, the cruise line canceled three upcoming voyages to implement enhanced sanitation measures, isolated affected individuals, and consulted the CDC’s Vessel Sanitation Program. The ship is currently heading to Ketchikan, Alaska. This outbreak follows three prior gastrointestinal illness events on the same vessel since late May, two of which were linked to norovirus.
analysis.summary_en: A gastrointestinal illness outbreak sickened 13 people—eight guests and five crew—aboard the National Geographic Sea Bird during a July 15 voyage, marking the vessel’s fourth such incident in under two months. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed the cases, which featured abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea, but the cause remains undetermined. In response, the cruise line canceled three upcoming voyages to implement enhanced sanitation measures, isolated affected individuals, and consulted the CDC’s Vessel Sanitation Program. The ship is currently heading to Ketchikan, Alaska. This outbreak follows three prior gastrointestinal illness events on the same vessel since late May, two of which were linked to norovirus.
